newsitem.title: ANTIGUA: CRICKET-LETHAL AMBROSE JOINS TEST ELITE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-LETHAL AMBROSE JOINS TEST ELITE.

text.p: Curtly Ambrose joined the exclusive club of test bowlers to have taken 300 test wickets as West Indies took the initiative on the first day of the first test against Sri Lanka on Friday.

Choosing his native island as a backdrop, Ambrose took five for 37 in just 13.1 overs to dismiss the Sri Lankans for 223 and become only the 12th bowler to reach the 300-wicket landmark, joining team-mate Courtney Walsh among the game's elite performers. At the close West Indies were 56-1.
Sri Lanka would have totalled far fewer without the efforts of opener Sanath Jayasuriya who made an excellent 85 from 115 balls and shared a fourth-wicket stand of 110 with captain Arjuna Ranatunga.

The touring side had made a terrible start to their first test on Caribbean soil as Ambrose ripped out three of the top four batsman with just 23 runs on the board, before Jayasuriya and Ranatunga temporarily steadied the ship in the afternoon.

Ranatunga was eventually run out for 42, beaten by Ambrose's throw from mid-off to wicket-keeper Courtney Browne as he attempted a single off a no-ball. Jayasuriya fell to off-spinner Carl Hooper having struck nine fours and two sixes.

At tea the Sri Lankans had reached 180 for five but middle-order batsman Hashan Tillekeratne failed to reappear after being forced to retire hurt on one when he was struck on the right forearm by a rising delivery by West Indies' skipper Walsh.
Ambrose returned to help mop up the tail in the final session, but it was his opening burst which set the day's tone after Walsh had won the toss.
Roshan Mahanama gave wicket-keeper Courtney Browne his 50th test dismissal in his 14th test before Russell Arnold fended his first ball to Stuart Williams at third slip.
Ambrose then captured the key wicket of Aravinda de Silva, caught at cover point without scoring by Walsh cutting at a short delivery.
